sentences.text: , therefore, if directions are issued to the Collector to decide the said application preferred by the present petitioner for referring the matter to the appropriate authority within a time bound frame, the grievance of the petitioner would come to an end.

3. On the contrary, Shri Praveen Newaskar, learned DSG for Railways submitted that the SDO vide Annexure P/1 had already observed in the report that the reliefs as claimed by the petitioner cannot be granted and, therefore, the application moved before the Collector for referring the matter to the appropriate authority is of no consequence and the petitioner is required to challenge the said report of the SDO before appropriate forum.
4.
Similar arguments has been raised by the learned Government Advocate and had submitted that the present petition is wholly mis- conceived and, therefore, is liable to be dismissed.

5. After hearing rival contentions and going through the reliefs as claimed, as well as Annexure P/1 which is a report dated 15.03.2024 from where it could be gathered that on directions of the Collector an enquiry had been conducted by the SDO with regard to the grievance of the petitioner and a report has been submitted thereon to the Collector, but till date Collector has not taken any decision as is required under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.
6.

Thus, in the fitness of things, this Court deems it appropriate to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:17414 3 WP-29015-2024 direct Collector to take decision on the application preferred by the present petitioner for referring the matter to appropriate authority under the Act of 2013.
7. With the aforesaid direction, the petition stands disposed of.
8. Let the aforesaid exercise be completed within a period of four weeks from today.

(MILIND RAMESH PHADKE) JUDGE Chandni Smt. Bhagwati Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36357817/

The present petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred seeking following reliefs:
1. Respondent no. 2 may kindly be directed to pass award under or order to reference to appropriate authority under section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013;
2. Respondents may kindly be directed to award appropriate compensation to petitioner for the trees acquired along with land;
3. Cost of the petition may kindly be allowed;
4. Any other relief that Hon'ble Court deems it fit in the facts and circumstances of the case may kindly be allowed.
2. At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner had made a limited prayer that the Collector may be directed to take appropriate decision as required under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Smt.
